title: Hattie McDaniel's birth chart
metaDescription: Hattie McDaniel's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 20.0° Gemini. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Four of the eight placements whose signs are settled stand in Gemini — the Sun, Mercury, Neptune and Pluto. The placements whose signs could change with an unknown hour are not counted. A cluster that size becomes the section the rest of the chart plays around.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: Measured rather than labelled, the Sun holds 20.0° Gemini: the third decan, whose classical sub-ruler is Saturn. An air sign, read here in its third face.

blocks.title: The personal registers
blocks.text: Day to day the chart speaks through Mercury in Gemini (26.8°), Mars in Cancer (17.7°): a mind at home in argument and pattern, drive that moves on certainty and current.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Mars to Jupiter is the closest call of the day, a sextile within 0.4°. The scheme reads a sextile as a door left unlocked. Useful, and entirely dependent on someone walking through it. Behind it, Neptune conjunction Pluto at 1.8°, and Saturn trine Pluto at 3.5° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. Each angle here was measured at every hour of the civil day and held; whatever the missing clock said, this geometry was in it.

blocks.title: Figures in the geometry
blocks.text: The Moon stands apart from every major angle the day held — the tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Of the seven planets the classical scheme judges, three sit in a sign it has an opinion about. Mercury in Gemini at 26.8° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Mars in Cancer at 17.7° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given; Saturn in Libra at 6.0° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best. Condition, not character: that is all the dignity table ever measured.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Of the 8 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: 5 in air, 2 in water, 1 in earth by element, 4 mutable, 2 cardinal, 2 fixed by modality. Air weights a chart toward language and pattern — the impulse to name a thing before deciding how to feel about it. Venus crossed from Gemini into Cancer during that day, so its sign is left open. No settled placement falls in fire — an absence the tradition treats as information, not as a defect. Uranus was retrograde — apparent backward motion from where the Earth sits, which the tradition reads as a function turned inward before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Aries into Taurus during that day at the birthplace, travelling 14.5° between one midnight and the next. Half the day belongs to each sign, and the split falls at an unrecorded hour — so this page holds the Moon as a genuine unknown.
